# Routing notes – SparkFun IoT RedBoard ESP32-P4 (4 layers)

Placement is untouched (`bt same` against the original: see the end). Only tracks, vias, zones, net classes were added. Read "Known weaknesses" before ordering: the board is fully connected and DRC-clean for copper, but parts of it are not what I would call finished work.

## Stack-up use

Stack-up as found: F.Cu / 0.1 mm prepreg / In1 / 1.24 mm core / In2 / 0.1 mm prepreg / B.Cu.

| layer | use |
|---|---|
| F.Cu | components, all controlled-impedance and fast routing that fits (DSI D0/D1, CSI D0/D1, flash QSPI, SDIO to the C5, USB full-speed, crystal, decoupling links, GPIO fan-out bus), GND pour in the gaps |
| In1 | solid GND plane, no tracks at all. Everything on F.Cu is 0.1 mm above it. |
| In2 | 3.3 V plane, with a GND area (higher priority zone) under the top-left quadrant where the high-speed pairs run on B.Cu. Round the processor it also carries tracks: 1.1 V distribution, three small LDO rails, flash Q/WP, and a number of short slow-signal hops (see weaknesses). |
| B.Cu | DSI CLK, CSI CLK, USB HS pairs (over the In2 GND area), SD bus, GPIO legs to the headers, supply trunks (5 V, VIN, VRAW, 3.3V_P), GND pour |

## Net classes (added to the .kicad_pro)

- Default: 0.15 mm track, 0.127 mm clearance, via 0.5/0.3.
- Power: 0.4 mm nominal (pads of fine-pitch parts force necks), via 0.6/0.3.
- USB: 0.15 mm / 0.13 mm gap ≈ 90 Ω differential on 0.1 mm prepreg (Hammerstad estimate, not field-solved).
- MIPI: 0.127 mm / 0.173 mm gap (0.3 mm pitch) ≈ 100 Ω. The 0.3 mm pitch was dictated by the gaps between the 0402s in front of the P4 pins: four tracks fit between C26/R33 and between R32/C27, not six.

Vias: 0.5/0.3 by default, 0.6/0.3 on supply trunks and thermal pads, 0.45/0.3 (the board's own minimum, 0.075 mm annular ring) for the ring vias under the QFN, between the decoupling columns and where nothing larger fits. Check that your fab accepts 0.45/0.3; everything else is relaxed.

## What was routed by hand and why

- **ESP32-P4 escape.** Every supply pin goes straight to its capacitor on F.Cu. Second-row capacitors are reached with 0.127 mm tracks through the 0.39 mm slots between first-row capacitors (the placement clearly intends this). Signals that must change layer use either a "ring via" between the pad row and the exposed pad, or a via just outside the pad row, alternating so adjacent pins never need two vias side by side.
- **MIPI DSI.** D0 enters J6 through the channel between the two staggered pad columns; D1 comes from the right with one leg passing between two pads of the near column. CLK cannot reach its pads with the right polarity on one layer (I worked the topology through for every approach), so it runs on B.Cu between ring vias and a via pair in the J6 channel, entering from the west so no twist is needed.
- **MIPI CSI.** D0/D1 on F.Cu up the corridor between J5 and J6 to the 100 Ω series resistors; CLK (resistors on the far side of J5) on B.Cu.
- **Skew.** `bt tune` matched all pairs within 0.01 mm except DSI D1 (1.5 mm left, ≈10 ps; no room for more bumps). Pair-to-pair matching was not attempted (lanes differ by a few mm; D-PHY tolerates that).
- **USB HS (OTG).** B.Cu from ring vias to the TVS, through the TVS pads on F.Cu, to the connector. A6/B6 are joined by a small loop round A7's end under the connector; test points get ≤2 mm stubs. USB serial/JTAG (full speed) is on F.Cu.
- **Flash.** D/CLK/HOLD and CS on F.Cu; Q/WP as 0.15 mm tracks on In2 (moved there from B.Cu so the east side of the chip stays open on B.Cu).
- **SDIO to the ESP32-C5.** Six parallel F.Cu tracks, arriving under the module from the south so the order matches; pull-ups directly above the module pads. Lengths 21…26 mm.
- **GPIO to the Arduino headers.** Pins 1–8 and IO0 fan out on F.Cu as a bus ending in a diagonal via row ordered like the header pins; the B.Cu legs then run north in order.
- **Power.** VIN, VRAW, 3.3V_P, 5 V as 0.45–0.6 mm B.Cu/F.Cu trunks (router, then checked). The LM66200 power-mux area was redone by hand after the router used 0.12 mm necks for the main supply path. Buck converter: short wide LX and output connections, FB sensed at the output capacitor.
- **Planes.** In1 GND solid. One GND via per capacitor at the P4 (placed between the two capacitor columns), 3×3 vias in the P4 exposed pad, vias in the flash and C5 pads. Outer-layer GND pours with thermal reliefs.

## Known weaknesses / not finished

1. **In2 round the processor is no longer a clean plane.** The SD bus on B.Cu fences off the bottom-left corner of the chip, and several nets could only be closed with hops on In2: ~RST (≈22 mm), SD_PWR, SD_DET, BAT_ST, IOA51, IOA53, JP2-B (charge LED), NET_RST, I2C SCL (to the fuel gauge, ≈20 mm round the buck), UART RX (6 mm), plus VDD_FLASH/VDD_MIPI/VDD_SD links. They are all slow, but each one is a slot in the 3.3 V plane, and the plane is cut into pockets near U1. I added explicit 3.3 V tracks wherever a decoupling via ended up in a pocket (the last routing step), so every pin is connected, but the 3.3 V impedance at the P4 is that of tracks and local capacitors, not of a plane. A cleaner solution needs the SD bus and the left-side pin escape redone together (all SD lines leaving the chip southwards), which I did not manage in the time.
2. **1.1 V core rail.** My first idea, an In2 island under the chip, does not work: the ring vias' antipads wall it in. 1.1 V is now routed as tracks (0.3–0.6 mm): directly from the inductor to the bottom-side pin (7 mm), and as a chain to the left pins and round the north side to the right-top pin (pin 26 is ≈55 mm from the inductor, estimated 60–90 mΩ). Each pin has its capacitor at the pin, so I expect it to work, but the DC drop to pin 26 and pin 54 should be checked against the P4 hardware design guide before production. This is the item I am least happy with.
3. **Slots under the B.Cu pairs.** Two In2 tracks (VDD_MIPI, VDD_FLASH, later also 1.1 V) run east–west just north of U1 and cross under the DSI CLK, CSI CLK and USB HS pairs; the UART RX hop crosses under DSI CLK at y≈90.5. Each is a ~0.6 mm gap in the pairs' reference plane (In1 GND is still continuous 1.3 mm further away). Acceptable for USB HS; for DSI/CSI clock at the highest rates I would want these moved.
4. **SD card bus is not length-matched**: 12…33 mm (CLK 27 mm, part of it on F.Cu). Fine for default/high-speed (25/50 MHz); not good enough for UHS-I.
5. **Long, via-rich slow nets** from the autorouter: I2C SDA (≈110 mm total copper, 12 vias), SCL, LED data (65 mm), UART0 (≈70 mm, 4–5 vias, one section along the top edge on F.Cu under the header pads), ~RST. They work electrically; they are not pretty and I2C/RST pick up more crosstalk than they should.
6. **VBATT into the LM66200** goes through a 0.7 mm long 0.127 mm neck between two capacitors (the only way to that pin without moving parts); 5 V reaches its pin through a via under the IC.
7. A few vias sit at the edge of 0402 pads (decoupling columns at U1, one in C28's pad, one between C38/C35). Tent them.
8. No impedance field-solve, no SI/PI simulation, and I had no GUI: everything was checked with KiCad DRC and renders.
9. Courtyard overlaps (12) and silkscreen-over-edge warnings are in the original placement and unchanged.

10. One cosmetic DRC warning remains (a 5 V track end that lands on its trunk mid-segment). The ESP32-C5 antenna keep-out is respected on all layers.

## Project file changes

- Net classes and patterns added (above).
- `min_resolved_spokes` lowered from 2 to 1: seven GND pads in tight spots get only one thermal spoke from the outer pours; each of them also has its own via or track to ground, so I relaxed the rule rather than make those pads solid.
- Nothing else in the rules was changed. The original board and project are kept in `/work/orig/`; my routing scripts are in `/work/tools/` (not needed to open the board).

## Verification (final file)

- `kicad-cli pcb drc` (KiCad 10.0.8, all severities, schematic parity on): **0 unconnected items, 0 parity issues**; 12 `courtyards_overlap` errors and 4 `silk_edge_clearance` warnings, all present in the board as received (connectors/standoffs overlapping by design); 1 `track_dangling` warning (item 10).
- `bt same orig/… new`: "nothing locked moved, no parts added or removed, pad nets unchanged".
- Copper: 1836 track segments (F.Cu 1.68 m, B.Cu 1.56 m, In2 0.31 m), 379 vias (196 × 0.5/0.3, 138 × 0.45/0.3, 45 × 0.6/0.3), 5 zones (GND on F/In1/B, 3.3 V and a GND area on In2). Narrowest track 0.122 mm (board minimum 0.12192).
- Pair lengths (mm): CSI CLK 17.79/17.79, CSI D0 17.91/17.91, CSI D1 15.21/15.21, DSI CLK 17.98/17.98, DSI D0 13.91/13.91, DSI D1 18.92/20.44, USB HS 38.7/39.7 (includes test-point stubs).
- In KiCad the inner layers are named L2.Cu (In1) and L3.Cu (In2), as in the original file.
